rows.requirement: Send \x1b[1m X \x1b[22m Y, verify the second cell has bold=false and dim=false .
rows.catalogueRequirement: In a headless backend, compare neutral C, bold/dim/italic X, and SGR 22 Y: bold and dim must clear while italic remains. Missing style readback makes the attempted reset check PROBE INVALID; a TTY cursor reply does not verify styling. App: before any attribute is set, draw YY and save with DECSC. For each of the seven nonempty subsets of bold, faint and italic, draw YY with the subset set, then restore with DECRC: every subset must change the crop and every restore must return it exactly. The italic-only crop must differ from the original and every other subset crop. Then set all three, draw YY, send the made-up SGR 99 and draw YY: the crop must not change. Send SGR 22 and draw YY. Supported: the crop equals the italic-only crop. Unsupported: the crop equals the original or a different subset crop. A change at the made-up SGR, or a crop matching neither, is PROBE INVALID. On a multiplexer a negative stays PROBE TODO naming the outer terminal. If a subset, restore or expected-crop separation does not qualify, DECRQSS decides, and a silent DECRQSS keeps the row named refusal.
rows.explanation: The current upstream catalogue adds a seven-subset App raster test with DECSC/DECRC and an SGR 99 negative control. Fresh stored bold/dim/italic flags satisfy the pinned parser criterion and the live page, but that newer App raster contract was not measured.

Missing setup readback makes the attempted reset check PROBE INVALID; a TTY cursor reply does not verify styling. App: before any attribute is set, draw YY and save with DECSC. For each of the seven subsets of bold, italic and inverse, draw YY with the subset set, then restore with DECRC: every subset must change the crop and every restore must return it exactly. Then set all three, draw YY, send the made-up SGR 99 and draw YY: the crop must not change. Send SGR 0 and draw YY. Supported: the crop equals the original. Unsupported: the crop equals a subset's crop. A change at the made-up SGR, or a crop matching neither, is PROBE INVALID. On a multiplexer a crop equal to a subset stays PROBE TODO naming the outer terminal. If a subset or restore does not qualify, DECRQSS decides, and a silent DECRQSS keeps the row's named refusal.

rows.requirement: Send ESC [ ? 25 l (DECTCEM reset) and verify the cursor is no longer visible.
rows.catalogueRequirement: Headless: measure initial visibility, establish a shown control, check the hidden state and verify restoration. App: with a measured raster, compare the cursor cell raw-pixel digest across shown, hidden and restored frames. Support needs the hidden digest to differ and the restored digest to equal the control; if the attempted check cannot establish a visible control or restored frame, it is PROBE INVALID. DECRQM mode 25 reports the state when no raster is available. If neither a measured raster nor usable DECRQM replies are available, the result is PROBE TODO: shown, hidden and restored frames are captured as evidence, and capture alone does not establish support.

rows.requirement: Send \x1b[?1049h ( DECSET 1049), verify altScreen mode is active.
rows.catalogueRequirement: App probe: query DECRPM for private mode 1049 with CSI ? 1049 $ p. Expected: DECRPM mode 1049 can be set. App arm: where DECRPM gives no reply or Ps 0, a controlled effect read in the same run decides: the effect appears with the mode set and not with it reset. A missing reply alone decides nothing and stays PROBE INVALID when no effect read is made.

rows.requirement: Send \x1b[?5h ( DECSCNM ), verify reverseVideo mode is active.
rows.catalogueRequirement: Library mode-state criterion: DECSET private mode 5, query DECRPM and read getMode, then DECRST, query and read again. Supported requires Ps 1 after set, Ps 2 after reset and getMode true then false. Ps 0, 2 or 4 after DECSET is Unsupported. No reply stays review PROBE TODO; null or disagreeing getMode and every other reply pair, including Ps 3, stay PROBE TODO. presentation (inverted frame) unmeasured; protocol measured. App protocol criterion: snapshot DECRPM mode 5. Ps 1 or 3 is Supported without mutation; Ps 4 is Unsupported without mutation. Ps 2 sends DECSET, queries again, then restores DECRST: Ps 1 or 3 is Supported; still Ps 2 is Unsupported (recognized but DECSET refused (mode kept reset)). Requires existing disposable-terminal authority. The DECRPM reply does not measure tearing, scroll cadence or the inverted frame. App arm: where DECRPM gives no reply or Ps 0, a controlled effect read in the same run decides: the effect appears with the mode set and not with it reset. A missing reply alone decides nothing and stays PROBE INVALID when no effect read is made.
rows.explanation: The stock trace only queries DECRPM 5 and receives Ps 2. It neither sends DECSET 5 nor observes Ps 1 followed by restored Ps 2. Recognition alone cannot satisfy the live-page activation or current catalogue transition criterion.

The DECRPM reply does not measure line wrapping (the headless probe measures wrapping separately). App arm: where DECRPM gives no reply or Ps 0, a controlled effect read in the same run decides: the effect appears with the mode set and not with it reset. A missing reply alone decides nothing and stays PROBE INVALID when no effect read is made.
rows.explanation: Mode-7 recognition remains separate; enabled and disabled writes use the same 85 bytes and compare observed cells and cursor.

rows.requirement: Apply bold+italic+inverse via \x1b[1;3;7m X then send \x1b[0m Y, verify the second cell has all attributes cleared.
rows.catalogueRequirement: Apply bold+italic+inverse via \x1b[1;3;7mX then send \x1b[0mY, verify the second cell has all attributes cleared. App: before any attribute is set, draw YY and save with DECSC. For each of the seven subsets of bold, italic and inverse, draw YY with the subset set, then restore with DECRC: every subset must change the crop and every restore must return it exactly. Then set all three, draw YY, send the made-up SGR 99 and draw YY: the crop must not change. Send SGR 0 and draw YY. Supported: the crop equals the original. Unsupported: the crop equals a subset's crop. A change at the made-up SGR, or a crop matching neither, is PROBE INVALID. On a multiplexer a crop equal to a subset stays PROBE TODO naming the outer terminal. If a subset or restore does not qualify, DECRQSS decides, and a silent DECRQSS keeps the row's named refusal.
rows.explanation: Fresh bold/italic/inverse cell reset passes the pinned and live-page tests. The current upstream App raster-matrix alternative is unmeasured; this report conservatively refuses to equate stored flags with that presentation criterion.
